🤖 Milestone 6: correction chosen and safe-bound rule

**What we did and why.** We compared six methods for training on older rollouts at two configured ages on Qwen3-0.6B, to choose a default for faster Snowball training at the same answer quality. The correction head-to-head (E4.3) ran twelve configurations for 96 optimizer updates each, all at training seed 17; the twelve composed seed-29 configurations never ran. Each consumed the same 6,144 prompt groups and 24,576 responses. We then scored the retained checkpoints on 2,009 held-out questions with eight stochastic responses per question, and recovered realised ages from native telemetry, while the safe-bound rule remains open.

**Results.** The held-out table contains 16,072 responses per configuration. Completed correctness requires a correct answer and a completed response; it is the endpoint used for selection.

| Method | Completed correctness at configured age 1 | At configured age 2 | Within-age rank, 1 → 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Behaviour clipping (`behavior_clip`) | 0.34308 | 0.44400 | 6 → 5 |
| Regular PPO, no correction (`regular_no_tis`) | 0.55090 | 0.65648 | 4 → 1 |
| Regular PPO plus capped importance sampling (`regular_tis`) | 0.59190 | 0.42422 | 2 → 6 |
| Regular PPO plus token masking (`regular_mask`) | 0.60895 | 0.61660 | 1 → 2 |
| Behaviour clipping plus token masking (`bc_mask`) | 0.56203 | 0.51574 | 3 → 4 |
| Regular PPO plus second-moment masking (`regular_m2`) | 0.37519 | 0.53304 | 5 → 3 |

The two configured ages produce distinct group-weighted consumed distributions in all six method pairs: group-weighted consumed-age means are 0.9583333 at configured age 1 and 2.3333333 at configured age 2, with group-weighted p95 values 2 and 3. The token-weighted measurements below are at **cohort preparation**, a different measurement point.

| Configuration | Configured age | Consumed-group mean / p95 | Preparation token-weighted mean / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `behavior_clip-a1` | 1 | 0.9583333 / 2 | 0.4708 / 1 |
| `behavior_clip-a2` | 2 | 2.3333333 / 3 | 1.8634 / 2 |
| `regular_no_tis-a1` | 1 | 0.9583333 / 2 | 0.4693 / 1 |
| `regular_no_tis-a2` | 2 | 2.3333333 / 3 | 1.8662 / 2 |
| `regular_tis-a1` | 1 | 0.9583333 / 2 | 0.4702 / 1 |
| `regular_tis-a2` | 2 | 2.3333333 / 3 | 1.8673 / 2 |
| `regular_mask-a1` | 1 | 0.9583333 / 2 | 0.4716 / 1 |
| `regular_mask-a2` | 2 | 2.3333333 / 3 | 1.8662 / 2 |
| `bc_mask-a1` | 1 | 0.9583333 / 2 | 0.4710 / 1 |
| `bc_mask-a2` | 2 | 2.3333333 / 3 | 1.8651 / 2 |
| `regular_m2-a1` | 1 | 0.9583333 / 2 | 0.4712 / 1 |
| `regular_m2-a2` | 2 | 2.3333333 / 3 | 1.8653 / 2 |

The preparation-time token distributions separate: the age-1 cells have no age-2 tokens, while the age-2 cells have about 93% of their tokens at age 2 and none at age 1. Both include age-zero tokens. The earlier uncertainty about whether the configured ages ever separated is resolved at these measurement points. **Token-weighted consumed age cannot be reconstructed:** the retained consumption aggregates lack a join between each group's age and token count. Within-cohort minibatch lag must not be substituted for consumed age.

The paired completed-correctness differences below compare each method with behaviour clipping at the same configured age. Intervals are simultaneous within each five-comparison family.

| Method | Difference at age 1 [interval] | Difference at age 2 [interval] |
|---|---:|---:|
| `regular_no_tis` | +0.20781 [+0.19033, +0.22611] | +0.21248 [+0.19375, +0.23152] |
| `regular_tis` | +0.24882 [+0.22779, +0.26960] | −0.01979 [−0.03347, −0.00585] |
| `regular_mask` | +0.26587 [+0.24558, +0.28671] | +0.17260 [+0.15599, +0.18853] |
| `bc_mask` | +0.21895 [+0.20110, +0.23762] | +0.07174 [+0.05986, +0.08344] |
| `regular_m2` | +0.03211 [+0.02066, +0.04331] | +0.08904 [+0.07305, +0.10484] |

These intervals resample paired questions **within one training run** per configuration and carry no training-seed variance. They therefore understate the uncertainty relevant to a new seed, a new age or Snowball. All displayed intervals exclude zero; the small negative importance-sampling interval still spans the −2-percentage-point reporting margin. Semantic correctness is not evaluable as a paired statistic because 44–715 responses per configuration are unresolved by Math-Verify, and those responses provide no evidence. The completed-correctness ordering also appears under greedy decoding, except that the two token-masking configurations tie; this uses the same training checkpoints.

Every configuration crossed the 0.1-nat policy-entropy threshold under the original any-excursion reading, as the [original correction result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649345549) reported. The written sustained-collapse rule is **ten consecutive optimizer updates with actual policy entropy strictly below 0.1 nats**. Recomputing all 96 updates in each of the twelve cells gives **12 passes, 0 failures**: the longest streak is five, in `regular_m2` at configured age 1, and every other cell's longest is at most two. The earlier 11/12 disposition is superseded by this recomputation. The second-seed configurations never ran.

**What this means.** **`regular_mask` wins the selector and is chosen for robustness.** It is the only method whose two configurations appear in the global top three; within each age it ranks first and second. The no-correction control moves from within-age fourth to first (global sixth to first), overtaking masking, capped importance sampling and behaviour clipping plus masking; capped importance sampling drops from within-age second to sixth (global fourth to tenth), and second-moment masking overtakes behaviour clipping plus masking. That instability argues against choosing the largest point estimate as a general correction rule.

The upcoming Snowball comparison spans staleness 0, 2 and 4, while this screen measured 1 and 2. Choosing regular PPO without correction would leave the highest-staleness arm unprotected and make a staleness knee indistinguishable from an uncorrected-training knee. We therefore carry `regular_mask` into every arm. What transfers is an ordering among corrections **not established at one seed**, from a 0.6B dense model to a 67B mixture of experts. It is an acceptable default to run with and cannot bear weight in the final claim; if confirmation hinges on correction choice, it needs its own seeds at Snowball scale.

The [historical indicator pilot](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5598170776) still supplies the safe-bound disposition: no predictive alert is adopted, the held-out-seed validation criterion remains untested, and health thresholds remain flags. This correction selection establishes neither a safe age range nor a Snowball speedup.

**Next.** Use `regular_mask` in all three Snowball development arms: the synchronous C1/A0 control on the same fast weight-sync path, the C1/A2 deep-pool arm and the C1/A4 deep-pool arm. Before writing the comparison, report masked-token fraction **per arm and per realised age**, and require it to be **near zero in the staleness-zero control**. If masking increasingly removes training tokens at higher age, the effective batch changes along the axis being measured; that must inform the interpretation. The correction default then carries into the final tradeoff statement, with its quality, wall-clock, GPU-hour and off-policy-age uncertainty.

🤖 Snowball used 43–53% less training wall time, with no quality winner at one seed

**What we did and why.** We tested whether overlapping answer generation with learning can make Snowball training faster while preserving completed-answer quality. This 100-update comparison (E9.1) used one training seed, 17, for a zero-age control and two configurations allowing answers to be up to two or four optimizer updates old. All three used the same runtime, 40 H100s, one weight copy per update, the selected parser and regular loss with mismatch masking; requests in flight were aborted at a weight copy. The age caps were bundled with 64, 96 and 160 generation workers respectively, so this compares complete configurations rather than isolating age alone.

**Results.** Completed correctness means a correct answer with an accepted stopping reason. These are the in-run development set's 256 questions, one evaluated response per question; the larger frozen held-out evaluation remains pending.

| Configuration | Completed at update 100 | Length-limited at update 100 | Difference from control | Simultaneous interval, percentage points |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Zero-age control | 130/256 = 50.78% | 101/256 = 39.45% | Reference | — |
| Age cap 2 | 68/256 = 26.56% | 153/256 = 59.77% | −24.22 pp | [−31.64, −16.80] |
| Age cap 4 | 112/256 = 43.75% | 122/256 = 47.66% | −7.03 pp | [−14.45, +0.78] |

The age-2 run ended **24.22 points below control**, with interval **[−31.64, −16.80]**, after a late decline into length-limited answers. Its point estimate falls outside the accepted 20-point outer bound; its interval lies wholly below the 15-point boundary and straddles the 20-point boundary, so neither non-inferiority bound is established. This is **one run**, the ordering across age caps is **non-monotone**, and the separately labelled keep-runtime control's two scored seeds differ by **13.7 points**; the three-seed confirmation is already under way. No configuration decision is made against age 2.

For age 4, the lower interval endpoint is above −15 points and therefore also above −20: the fixed-seed development interval excludes losses of both 15 and 20 points. This does not establish population non-inferiority across training seeds. Its Holm-adjusted p-value is 0.0440 while its Bonferroni simultaneous interval includes zero; these use different multiplicity corrections, so neither statistic alone supports a blanket claim of a quality difference or equivalence. Age 2's Holm-adjusted p-value is 0.0002.

The full completed-answer curves, in counts out of 256, show why the endpoint should not be read as a stable ordering:

| Update | Zero-age control | Age cap 2 | Age cap 4 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 36 | 40 | 38 |
| 20 | 88 | 84 | 92 |
| 40 | 112 | 91 | 94 |
| 60 | 120 | 94 | 98 |
| 80 | 122 | 91 | 54 |
| 100 | 130 | 68 | 112 |

The control rises throughout. Age 2 peaks at update 60 and then falls; age 4 dips to 54 completed answers at update 80 while 181/256 answers hit the length limit (70.70%), then ends at 112. That last rise is not evidence of a continuing recovery trend. These are scorer-recomputed curves: updates 20–100 match the runtime exactly; at update 0 the scorer finds two additional completed answers per arm in the level-4 view, a disclosed verifier-mapping discrepancy. The pre-registered endpoint stays at 100.

| Configuration | Training wall (s) | Core (s) | Task GPU-hours | Consumed response/loss tokens | Masked-token fraction | Realised age p50 / p95 / max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Zero-age control | 6,234.936 | 5,199.663 | 76.724753 | 11,346,279 | 0.160394% | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Age cap 2 | 3,544.291 | 2,474.043 | 46.803118 | 12,113,506 | 0.145263% | 1 / 2 / 2 |
| Age cap 4 | 2,942.138 | 1,803.606 | 40.303989 | 12,569,651 | 0.170717% | 3 / 4 / 4 |

Relative to control, age 2 reduced training wall by 43.15%, core time by 52.42% and task GPU-hours by 39.00%; age 4 reduced them by 52.81%, 65.31% and 47.47%. Training wall spans update 1's start through update 100's cycle; core sums the 100 reported core intervals. Task GPU-hours include each original child task's setup and teardown, so they are not simply training wall times 40. Masking is selected-token weighted and age quantiles are response-token weighted. Every consumed control token was age 0, and its masked fraction was near zero.

**What this means.** The measured time and resource reductions are substantial, but one run per configuration does not select a quality winner or establish that age 2 is unsafe. Earlier same-configuration replicates put development-set noise near 5 percentage points. Separately, the keep-runtime control scored 85/256 and 50/256 across seeds 17 and 29, a 13.67-point range; with one run per seed this mixes seed and run variability. That range motivates the 15-point confirmation margin and 20-point outer bound, but a wider margin does not fix late-training instability.

Those keep-runtime runs are not pooled with this abort-runtime control. The source audit shows that a group's version is stamped at generation start and that keep mode can admit a group spanning a weight copy as nominal age 0; elevated tail-token mismatch is consistent with that mechanism. This corrects the earlier assumption that pause mode could affect only wall time at age 0. The runtimes differ by more than pause mode, so the same-seed 17.58-point control gap cannot be attributed to that mechanism. Discard rates were not exported to run history and cannot be recovered from these histories.

**Next.** Finish the three-seed confirmation (E9.2) on one common abort runtime, retaining these three seed 17 runs and adding seeds 29 and 43 at all three age caps. At this draft's evidence cutoff, all six additional members are submitted; both new zero-age control coordinators and both 40-H100 children are running after independent startup review and authenticated CPU preflight. All six continue to completion. The confirmation will report both non-inferiority bounds and achieved power; no achieved multi-seed power is claimed from the present one-seed result. Complete the frozen held-out panels and investigate the late length-limit instability, then make the quality–wall-time–GPU-hour decision from the audited confirmation rather than selecting the best curve here.

🤖 Retaining the generation cache saved 2.1% of training wall time and missed the 10% adoption gate

**What we did and why.** We tested whether a deeper pool of answers and keeping generation alive across weight copies could support faster Snowball training at the same answer quality. The deep-pool experiment (E5.8) compared abort and cache-retaining keep at maximum ages two and four, with 96 and 160 generation workers respectively and a 32-group completed buffer. All four configurations used 32 learner and 8 inference H100s, one weight copy per update, one training seed and a 25-update endpoint. Age allowance, workers and buffer changed together relative to the historical age-one reference, so this tests a bundle.

The bundle is not quality-neutral: pinning the buffer alone changes nothing admitted; raising workers pushes realised age up within the cap; raising the allowance raises the cap. In the correction screen, configured ages one and two had group-weighted mean consumed ages of 0.958 and 2.333. The comparisons at staleness zero, two and four are designed to price that trade.

**Results.** Three members completed 25 updates: both abort arms and age-four keep. Age-two keep ended in operational failure after four accepted training updates, preemption and repeated rejection by the existing measurement guard; restarted evaluations cannot be spliced into a completed run. It supplies no update-25 quality or matched keep comparison.

| Matched age-four comparison | Abort | Keep with cache retained |
|---|---:|---:|
| Training wall to update 25 | 769.8 s | 753.6 s |
| Core time | 552.4 s | 542.0 s |
| Mean generation-buffer wait | 6.579 s/update | 6.420 s/update |
| Maximum reported consumed-group age | 3 | 3 |
| Completed-correct answers at update 25 | 51/256 = 19.92% | 37/256 = 14.45% |
| Length-limited answers at update 25 | 165/256 = 64.45% | 152/256 = 59.38% |

Keep reduced wall time by **2.103%**, below the required **10%**. Both quality scores clear the approved historical development-score floor; the earlier interpretation as a two-sided window is superseded. Keep exceeded the matched abort band's range in 12 of 51 monitored quantities, with the largest excursion 1.39 band widths. No consumed age exceeded its cap and no non-finite step was found in the matched pair.

The descriptive keep-minus-abort quality difference is **−5.469 percentage points**, simultaneous interval **[−10.55, −0.3906]**, Holm-adjusted p=0.04140. This is one run per arm on 256 development questions. Two abort runs of the same age-two configuration and seed differed by **5.078 points** at update 5, interval **[−9.766, −0.3906]**, and by 1.953 points at both update 0 and update 25. Even at identical initial weights, 33 of 256 completed-answer bits differed. Keep did not beat abort and may be worse; these observations do not establish a 5.5-point quality cost attributable to keep.

The full completed-answer curves make that variability visible:

| Configuration | Update 0 | Update 5 | Update 25 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Age-two abort, final member | 44/256 | 47/256 | 34/256 |
| Age-two abort, separate earlier replicate | 39/256 | 34/256 | 29/256 |
| Age-four abort | 40/256 | 31/256 | 51/256 |
| Age-four keep | 35/256 | 34/256 | 37/256 |

Both age-two abort runs degrade from their initial score, ending with approximately 73% and 82% length-limited answers, while age-four abort rises overall. This non-monotone one-seed ordering supplies no causal age ranking. Semantic means condition on different resolved subsets: at update 25 they are 94.87% over 78 resolved rows for abort and 90.10% over 101 for keep, each out of 256 questions. Unresolved rows are no evidence; these means are not a paired or comparable quality ranking.

The drift excursions are retained rather than compressed into a binary label:

| Monitored quantity | Keep updates outside abort range, out of 25 | Largest excursion, in abort-range widths |
|---|---:|---:|
| Lower clipping pressure | 19 | 1.390 |
| Absolute log-ratio p99 | 12 | 0.887 |
| First-256 selected-token count | 6 | 0.837 |
| Last-256 selected-token count | 6 | 0.837 |
| Upper clipping pressure | 12 | 0.717 |
| Absolute log-ratio p95 | 12 | 0.675 |
| Maximum absolute log-ratio | 2 | 0.439 |
| Mean squared log-ratio | 2 | 0.408 |
| Token-weight effective sample-size fraction | 1 | 0.212 |
| Mean log-ratio | 1 | 0.163 |
| Absolute log-ratio p50 | 1 | 0.021 |
| Mean absolute log-ratio | 1 | 0.001 |

The two selected-token counts reflect packing, not drift. The other 39 monitored quantities stayed within the observed abort range. This range is an empirical one-run reference, not a population uncertainty interval.

**What this means.** Retain abort. Mechanically, abort does **not** throw away the generated answer: the unbatched retry path retains tokens and their sampled log-probabilities, prepends them to the retry and reduces the remaining token budget. It loses the key-value cache and rebuilds it in a parallel prefill, rather than decoding the prefix again. The earlier claim that pausing discards about 30% of generated tokens was wrong. Keep with cache clearing has little work to save; the tested cache-retaining variant lets new weights read a cache built by old weights, with no coherent policy reference for that computation. Per-token sampled log-probabilities already support correction of mixed-version sequences; missing version tags or another correction do not repair stale cache state.

PipelineRL and Magistral report stale-cache continuation as workable in their systems; this conclusion concerns this system's arithmetic and measurement, not a universal impossibility.

The wall gate fails independently of the noisy quality comparison, and the drift excursions provide an additional reason not to adopt cache-retaining keep. The pool evidence is narrower: buffer wait falls from about 22.7 s/update in the historical age-one reference to 15.39 at age two and 6.579 at age four, but those changes cannot be apportioned among age, workers and buffer. The reference predates the fast weight-copy path, so this is not a clean total-wall speedup. The age-two pool rule required wait below 6.0 s/update and was not met.

**Next.** Carry abort into the same-runtime, three-seed quality and cost confirmation, with no age-two rejection or age-four winner inferred here. The separate buffer-only arm has completed 25 updates: mean buffer wait is 20.85 s/update, core time 899.2 s and task cost 19.72 GPU-hours, with token-age p95 of one. Its quality join remains pending, and without a matched unpinned reference on the same sync path it does not isolate a causal buffer benefit. An additional engine is not adopted from these results; its conditional sustained-idle trigger needs its own measurement. The next milestone is **system balance measured**.

🤖 Milestone 8: system balance measured; none of three inference allocations met the 20% time-saving gate

**What we did and why.** Since the [weight-sync milestone](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5652831170), we combined worker-allocation, cadence, admission and generation experiments to choose settings for faster Snowball training at the same answer quality. This synthesis includes measured negatives, completed development-score joins and explicit unmeasured cases. These balance experiments support the operational configuration used in the subsequent confirmation; alone, they do not establish a quality-preserving Snowball speedup or a winning off-policy age.

**Results.** At maximum age two, none of the three inference allocations meets both the frozen 20% wall-reduction requirement and the limit of 5% additional task GPU-hours relative to the age-one reference.

| Learner / inference GPUs | Age cap | Wall to 25 updates (s) | Core (s) | Task GPU-hours | Completed at update 25 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 / 8 reference | 1 | 1,132.5 | 920.2 | 20.14 | 25/256 |
| 32 / 8 | 2 | 961.4 | 750.7 | 18.06 | 51/256 |
| 32 / 16 | 2 | 944.5 | 748.4 | 21.42 | 24/256 |
| 32 / 24, proof cost subtracted | 2 | 957.6 | 770.0 | 25.39 | 40/256 |

The three-engine row subtracts 665.4 seconds of measured training-time byte proofs and another 27.14 seconds of startup proof from allocation accounting. It holds the observed schedule and waits fixed: it is an algebraic adjustment to a proofs-on run, not a measured proofs-off execution. Its adjusted wall reduction is 15.44% and GPU-hour increase 26.08%; the corrected row still fails both requirements. The one-engine age-two row saves 15.11% wall and 10.32% task GPU-hours, missing the wall gate. Scores are one-seed development observations, not evidence that one allocation has better population quality.

The broader balance results are consistent with retaining simple defaults:

| Experiment | Audited finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| [Initial small-model throughput fit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5638763417) | Three trainer predictions miss by 28.7–37.7%; the serving fit is degenerate | No split recommendation |
| [Bounded-queue small-model fit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5639305274) | Four nominal prediction checks pass, but concurrency coverage fails | No validated serving-capacity curve |
| [Standalone serving curve](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649728781) | All four trainer predictions miss the 15% requirement | Does not transfer as a split selector |
| [Extra inference GPUs at age one](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5652830847) | Core time falls 4.224%, task GPU-hours rise 15.80% | Retain 32 learner / 8 inference GPUs |
| [Serving-knob screen](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649672433) | No changed setting clears both speed tests; the frozen quality veto remains unevaluable | Defaults retained; evidence-contract failure reported |
| [Newest-first admission](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649684739) | Mean group age falls 0.11–0.17 updates, with no core-time gain in either matched seed | No winner; FIFO remains default |
| [Speculative decoding](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649684860) | Five-token proposals save 0.5230% core time and worsen rollout-group p95 by 20.05% | Misses the joint 10% requirement; speculation stays off |
| [Interrupted-rollout qualification](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649753804) | Consumed prompt-set digests differ on seven of eight updates | Qualification failed; the dependent partial-rollout experiment is offloaded |
| [Independent-family cost-model check](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5654100000) | Prediction errors are +44.59% and +9.441% at 8 and 16 inference GPUs | Only one geometry passes; no validated optimum |
| [Length-adjusted age analysis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5654169399) | Aggregate slope +0.9084 pp/age, conditional 95% interval [−3.487, +4.251] | Individual stratification and sequential replay remain unmeasured; no age recommendation |

The new scoring synthesis covers all 14 members and 50 evaluation points of the two cadence studies and the age-two allocation study. It reuses the completed Snowball cadence joins rather than rerunning them. On the small model, completed correctness at update 96 averaged 62.11%, 60.16%, 57.03% and 60.94% for copy cadences one, two, four and eight. That cadence-eight average mixes the retained first-attempt seed-17 run with a second-attempt seed-29 run, so its two seeds do not come from one physical campaign. Population intervals for the differences from cadence one are respectively [−10.94, +7.031], [−12.89, +2.344] and [−9.375, +7.031] percentage points for the latter three settings. All include zero at two seeds; neither a cadence effect nor equivalence is established. The cadence-eight setting also changes its age cap.

The one-seed Snowball cadence endpoints are 20/256, 11/256 and 19/256 completed answers at update 25 for copies every one, two and four updates; the last also changes the age cap. These are development scores with different questions from the small-model battery. Likewise, newest-first admission's fixed-seed gain of 4.88 points has a population interval [−3.52, +13.67] at two seeds: it does not select an admission-order winner. Later development joins close the speculative-decoding dump gap but do not turn its failed timing gate into adoption or establish held-out equivalence.

The [deep-pool experiment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5660856073) adds a direct pause-mode result: at age four, retaining the generation cache reduced wall time from 769.8 to 753.6 seconds, **2.103% against a 10% gate**, and 12 of 51 monitored quantities left the abort range. The observed keep-minus-abort quality difference is −5.469 points, interval [−10.55, −0.3906], but same-configuration replicates differed by 5.078 points at one evaluation. Keep did not beat abort and may be worse; this is not a demonstrated 5.5-point quality cost. Age-two keep never completed after four accepted updates and guard-rejected restarts, so no endpoint is filled in for it.

**What this means.** The balance decision is to copy once per update and use 32 learner and 8 inference GPUs, FIFO admission, speculation off and abort at weight copy. These were the operational choices taken into the confirmation. The allocation timing-and-cost screen rejects every proposed engine increase; keep fails its wall gate; the one-seed deep-pool evidence does not select between age two and age four. The cadence choice is an operational ruling, with no claim of quality equivalence and no new cadence experiment required.

Abort resubmits interrupted answers with their tokens and sampled log-probabilities; it rebuilds the key-value cache by prefill rather than discarding and decoding the answer again. The old “about 30% of tokens discarded by pause” claim is withdrawn. Cache-retaining keep saves that prefill but lets new weights read old-weight cache state, which does not provide a coherent policy reference. Per-token version tags are telemetry, not a repair for this defect.

Pool wait fell from roughly 22.7 to 15.4 to 6.6 seconds per update across the historical reference and the age-two/age-four abort bundles. Age allowance, worker count and buffer all moved, so that comparison cannot assign the change to a single knob or establish a matched total-wall speedup. The later buffer-only arm and its matched unpinned twin both completed: summed cycle time differs by only about 0.1%, one run per arm. That supports attributing the bundle benefit to allowance and workers rather than buffer pinning alone at this shape; it does not establish a precise effect or quality equivalence. The completed buffer-only development join likewise establishes no quality difference against its historical reference.

Carry the other negatives forward: the 16-learner FP32- and BF16-gradient recipes exhausted memory before an update, and [BF16 gradient reduction at the working geometry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5653217865) lengthened the measured training phase by 6.508%. Tensor-parallel decode, FP8 cache, larger sequence capacity and faster MoE kernels retain their recorded placement or implementation exclusions; those are not new GPU comparisons.

**Next.** The [subsequent three-seed confirmation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5662695626) and [final tradeoff statement](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5663169886) now carry the age/worker/buffer decision and its quality and performance uncertainty. Matched-seed age-one comparisons, held-out evaluation and full resource accounting continue as follow-ups. The offloaded MoE-rung work remains unevaluated. The next numbered milestone after this balance synthesis is **final tradeoff statement**, now posted.

<details><summary>Provenance</summary>

This is the completed balance synthesis with the accepted decisions and remaining evidence limits stated explicitly. The deep-pool group's four member dispositions are audited and posted: three update-25 completions and one operational non-completion, with no missing endpoint imputed. The two cadence studies have completed development joins; the allocation study has completed development joins and a negative proof-corrected timing decision. Their historical card audits still lack some required deliverables, and no separate experiment-comment URL for those three groups was found at the repair read. This synthesis does not claim those audit checklists or missing standalone posts are complete.

The historical inventory and readiness audit predate these scoring and publication results. Their earlier missing-join statements do not describe the current evidence. Retained provenance still lacks the complete historical cadence table/plot and overlay, locally enumerated per-point scoring hashes and individual first-token stamps; the new-cadence remeasurement is not treated as having run. Those limits qualify the historical card, while the operational cadence ruling stands. Local result-file links from the earlier public body have been replaced by public experiment links and the exact source hashes below.

The allocation comparison uses Snowball seed 17, C1/N1, 25 updates and the frozen age-one reference. Exact proof-subtracted values are 957.645524908005 wall seconds, 769.982186026027 core seconds and 25.390194480464 task GPU-hours; limits are 905.996238401532 seconds and 21.145821666667 GPU-hours. Raw three-engine execution remains 1,623.034115442019 wall seconds and 36.162884444444 task GPU-hours; no causal schedule replay or observed proofs-off three-engine result is claimed.

The cadence bootstrap uses seed 1729, 10,000 replicates, family alpha 0.05, Bonferroni simultaneous percentile intervals and Holm-adjusted p-values. Qwen cadence has two training seeds; both Snowball studies have one. Seven Qwen terminal manifests are absent under the accepted detached-finalizer exception; the scoring receipt explicitly records model-identity fallback and direct W&B evaluation-history scans after the older training-metric audit refuses those runs. Tokenizer checks and dump/W&B evaluation parity remain enforced. Original policy-payload hashes remain unavailable. At cadence four, consumed age five reflects admission age at most four plus within-cohort lag of at most one; cadence-eight seed 29 retains 640 stale-group rejections. These limitations and the accepted detached-finalizer exception remain attached to the result.

The deep-pool timing and quality claims retain their exact final-family attempt boundaries. Abort/keep run on their named historical runtimes, not the later parser-only confirmation pin; the separate earlier age-two abort replicate is not promoted to the final family. The approved quality screen is a floor, which both completed age-four arms pass. Of the 12 out-of-range quantities, two are selected-token packing counts rather than drift.

🤖 Three-seed Snowball confirmation: age four meets the 15-point quality margin; age two remains unresolved

**What we did and why.** We confirmed whether overlapping generation and learning can deliver faster Snowball training at the same answer quality, comparing a zero-age control with deep generation pools allowing answers up to two or four updates old (E9.2). Each configuration has matched training seeds 17, 29 and 43, with 100 updates on the same abort runtime and 40 H100s: 32 learner and 8 inference GPUs. All copy weights once per update, use parser-only stopping and regular loss with mismatch masking; the age caps are bundled with 64, 96 and 160 generation workers respectively, so this compares complete configurations. An added age-one deep-pool configuration at three seeds was submitted at 10:37 UTC and is reported when it lands.

**Results.** Completed correctness means a correct answer with an accepted stopping reason. These results use the in-run development set of 256 questions, one response per question, at the pre-registered update-100 endpoint. Held-out update-100 comparisons remain pending.

| Configuration | Seed 17 | Seed 29 | Seed 43 | Mean completed correctness | Mean difference from control | Primary population interval, pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Zero-age control | 50.78% | 43.75% | 53.52% | 49.35% | Reference | — |
| Age cap one | Pending | Pending | Pending | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Age cap two | 26.56% | 48.83% | 46.48% | 40.63% | −8.72 pp | [−25.39, +6.25] |
| Age cap four | 43.75% | 43.36% | 53.13% | 46.74% | −2.60 pp | [−9.77, +3.91] |

The population intervals resample both seeds and questions and account for the two tested async configurations. The corresponding fixed-observed-seed intervals are [−12.50, −4.95] points for age two and [−6.38, +1.17] for age four; those conditional intervals cannot establish a claim about new training seeds. The population intervals are primary.

| Configuration | One-sided lower bound, pp | Excludes a loss of 15 pp? | Excludes a loss of 20 pp? | Paired-difference SD | Achieved power at 15 / 20 pp |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| Age cap two | −33.54 | No | No | 14.72 pp | 32.9% / 46.8% |
| Age cap four | −9.07 | Yes | Yes | 3.83 pp | 98.9% / 100.0% |

Age four is non-inferior at the 15-point margin. Age two is **neither shown inferior nor shown non-inferior at 15 or 20 points**: its three differences are −24.22, +5.08 and −7.03 points, leaving three seeds under-powered to resolve it. Age four's differences are −7.03, −0.39 and −0.39 points. Both conclusions have the same limitation: with three seeds and two degrees of freedom, the estimated spread is imprecise and cannot distinguish a consistently tight configuration from a lucky sample. The power figures describe this sample under a true difference of zero, not an enduring property of either configuration.

The same-runtime control's observed SD is 5.04 points and range 9.77 points. The separately labelled keep-runtime control spans 26.56 points across three seeds; its earlier two-seed range was 13.67 points when the 15-point margin and 20-point outer bound were set. That spread explains the wider margin, but does not repair instability. The pre-observation unpaired model assumed 10-point per-run spread and gives 52.6% / 71.2% power at the two margins; the paired results above use each configuration's measured paired-difference spread instead.

| Configuration and seed | Training wall, seconds | Measured-attempt task GPU-hours | All-attempt task GPU-hours | Execution accounting |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Zero-age, 17 | 6,234.936 | 76.724753 | 76.724753 | Child terminal audited |
| Zero-age, 29 | Pending | Pending | Pending | Update-100 dumps scored; final accounting pending |
| Zero-age, 43 | 6,342.002 | 78.018964 | 78.018964 | Child terminal audited |
| Age two, 17 | 3,544.291 | 46.803118 | 46.803118 | Child terminal audited |
| Age two, 29 | 3,475.846 | 46.031298 | At least 46.816578 | Child terminal audited; earlier allocation endpoints incomplete |
| Age two, 43, retry | Pending | Pending | Pending | Update-100 dumps scored; final accounting pending |
| Age four, 17 | 2,942.138 | 40.303989 | 40.303989 | Child terminal audited |
| Age four, 29 | 2,904.269 | 39.707851 | 40.447218 | Child terminal audited; startup preemption included |
| Age four, 43 | 2,784.402 | 38.710644 | 38.710644 | Child terminal audited |

In the retained seed-17 comparison, age four used **52.81% less training wall time and 47.47% fewer task GPU-hours**, approximately 53% and 47%, than the synchronous zero-age control. Those are the earlier seed-17 durations; the confirmation's own per-member measurements are reported above. They are not three-seed performance estimates or confidence intervals. Training wall runs from update one's start through update 100's cycle; task GPU-hours sum individual allocations including setup and teardown. The two jobs still in final accounting are not declared terminal merely because their scored endpoints exist. The original age-two seed-43 run stalled at update 55 and was operationally superseded by a science-identical retry; its prefix is not pooled into the retry's quality trajectory, and campaign-wide resource cost remains incomplete.

Late-training instability remains an open defect. In the seed-17 development curves, age two peaked at 94/256 completed answers at update 60 and ended at 68/256, with 153/256 length-limited answers. Age four dipped to 54/256 at update 80 with 181/256 length-limited answers, then ended at 112/256; the endpoint does not prove a continuing recovery. Several later confirmation runs improve through training, so collapse is not universal. The longer answer-stopping qualification also failed its under-10% truncation criterion, reaching 94.14% truncation at the control endpoint and 94.53% in the other completed run at update 80.

The first frozen held-out panel, at the initial weights, has now been scored: **3,012/13,176 = 22.860%** completed correct under the frozen contract, beside **2,812/13,176 = 21.342%** in the runtime aggregate. The 200-response, 1.52-point gap comes from normally terminated correct answers whose boxed or numerical formatting the runtime parser rejects; frozen-rule scoring remains the reported measure and the runtime parity failure is disclosed. This initial panel is not a trained-checkpoint comparison. A descriptive read of retained training dumps withdrew the hypothesis that parser under-crediting drives late collapse: the disagreement largely disappears by update 20, before the collapse. Parser normalization remains a correction for the next campaign, not an established cause of instability.

**What this means.** The chosen configuration for the final tradeoff statement is **copy every update, age cap four, deep pool, abort**, with the stopping and correction packages as run. It establishes development-set non-inferiority at the 15-point margin on three seeds, alongside the labelled seed-17 time and resource reductions. Age two remains unresolved; no decision against it follows from its unlucky seed-17 result. Age one is pending, and the measured settings do not establish a continuous safe-age range or isolate age from the worker and buffer changes.

The keep-runtime controls are never pooled with the same-runtime abort controls. Source inspection shows that keep can admit a group spanning one weight copy at nominal age zero; stage three shares that caveat. The runtimes differ beyond pause mode, so the endpoint effect cannot be assigned to keep alone. Neither the wider margin nor the chosen endpoint makes the answer-stopping defect fixed.

**Next.** Finish native terminal and resource accounting for the remaining two members, append the three age-one results when their receipts arrive, and attach the frozen held-out update-100 panels as they are scored on retained checkpoints. Age one's launch receipt and landing estimate are pending; no running state or invented ETA is claimed. Investigate late-training instability first after this reporting checkpoint. The next milestone is the **final tradeoff statement**, with completed quality, wall-time and GPU-hour intervals and the unresolved results kept explicit.

🤖 Milestone 4: answer-stopping criterion not met after 100 updates

**What we did and why.** Faster Snowball training at the same answer quality requires
answers that finish reliably. We tested the answer-stopping package and training-task
selection, following the earlier
[stopping diagnosis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5602358349)
and [task-selection result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649777019).
The five-package screen selected parser-only under its frozen ranking rule. The longer
confirmation therefore placed that same package in both the selected-package and control
positions at seeds 17 and 29; the position names do not create a treatment difference.

**Results.** In the screen, parser-only completed 100 of 256 questions correctly, versus
97 for forced closure, 95 for negative truncation advantage, 94 for soft overlong penalties
and 68 for repetition stopping. This was one seed at update 25. Only repetition stopping
was statistically separated from parser-only under the simultaneous comparisons:
its difference was −12.50 percentage points, with 95% simultaneous interval [−19.14, −6.250].
The three-question lead over forced closure does not establish a better package.

Two longer runs reached update 100, saved native checkpoints and wrote all six planned
development evaluations. Three other retained original attempts stopped operationally at
updates 61, 19 and 17. Their measured prefixes remain in the record; retries supplied no
scientific rows and missing endpoints are not filled in.

Both complete runs are now scored. Their full curves are below, with 256
responses at each evaluation. Completed correctness requires both a correct answer and
an accepted stopping reason.

| Run and metric | Update 0 | 20 | 40 | 60 | 80 | 100 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Seed 17, control position: completed correct | 15.62% | 33.59% | 32.81% | 17.97% | 12.11% | 1.95% |
| Seed 17, control position: length stopped | 57.03% | 52.73% | 48.44% | 72.66% | 80.08% | 94.14% |
| Seed 29, selected-package position: completed correct | 17.58% | 33.20% | 21.88% | 8.98% | 1.95% | 21.09% |
| Seed 29, selected-package position: length stopped | 54.30% | 49.61% | 67.97% | 86.72% | 94.53% | 71.88% |

**The less-than-10% truncation criterion is not met at any evaluation point in either run,
including update zero, where both exceed 54%.** At update 100, the control has 241/256
length-stopped responses and only 5/256 completed correct. The other run reaches 242/256
length-stopped responses at update 80. Both peak in completed correctness at update 20
and collapse afterward; seed 29 partially rebounds by update 100, so the decline is not
monotone. These are development measurements, with one completed run per position and
seed, not held-out evidence or a population treatment-effect interval.

**What this means.** The outcome is **criterion not met**: parser-only does not hold
truncation below the target through 100 updates, and the answer contract is not fixed.
The stage-two selector result stays unchanged. That mechanical choice did not establish
superiority, and the two completed long-run positions contain the same package on different
seeds; they do not supply a treatment contrast.

The runtime qualification matters. Stage 3 used the same keep runtime as the earlier
control-seed experiment, while the package screen used abort. Under keep, a group spanning
a weight copy can still be admitted at nominal age zero, and the recorded likelihood
mismatch is larger toward the response tail. The compared runtimes differ in more than
pause behavior, so the size of any quality effect cannot be assigned to keep alone.
Abort/resubmit retains generated tokens and their sampled log probabilities; it loses the
cache and requires re-prefill. These observations do not establish a measured discard rate
or a fixed quality cost of that re-prefill.

Two of the separately measured keep-runtime controls also fell after their earlier peaks:
seed 17 from 42.97% to 33.20% completed correctness, and seed 29 from 40.63% to 19.53%.
The third seed ends at 46.09%, making the complete three-seed range 26.56 percentage points.
This is labelled **keep-runtime control spread**, with one run per seed, never pooled into
the same-runtime abort control. It mixes seed and run effects; the separate replicate
experiment measured about 5 percentage points of run-to-run variation. Neither the range
nor the decline proves that keep caused the endpoint loss.

**Next.** Report stage three as criterion not met and retain the operational partials
without filling their missing endpoints or relaunching stage three. Late-training
instability is the first post-window fix. The descriptive parser timeline withdrew the
hypothesis that reward under-crediting drives the late collapse: that disagreement largely
vanishes by update 20, before the collapse. The next investigation must establish the
cause rather than treating that withdrawn hypothesis as a finding. The next numbered
milestone, [weight installation below 0.55 seconds](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5652831170),
is already posted; its publication preceded this answer-contract confirmation.

🤖 Milestone 10: age cap four preserves development quality at the approved margin, with a faster measured run

**What we did and why.** We combined the qualified weight-transfer path with the selected stopping and correction packages, then compared synchronous and asynchronous Snowball training at the same runtime over three matched training seeds. The [confirmation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5662695626) selects **copy every update, age cap four, deep pool, abort, `parser_only`, `regular_mask`**. This is a class T configuration tradeoff (a measured trade, not a free win) established by a class R confirmation; the transport improvements below are class X, byte-exact with no science change. The [answer-stopping qualification](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5662695825) failed, so the conclusion is limited to the measured development endpoint. Late-training instability remains the first post-window problem to fix.

**Results.** At update 100 on the same 256 development questions, completed correctness requires a correct answer and an accepted stopping reason. Three matched seeds give the following results; the confidence intervals resample seeds and questions and account for both tested asynchronous configurations.

| Configured age cap | Mean completed correctness | Difference from control | Primary 95% population interval | Non-inferiority at 15 / 20 pp |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Zero, synchronous control | 49.35% | Reference | — | Reference |
| One, deep pool | Running | Pending | Pending | Pending |
| Two, deep pool | 40.63% | −8.72 pp | [−25.39, +6.25] pp | Not established / not established |
| Four, deep pool, chosen | 46.74% | −2.60 pp | [−9.77, +3.91] pp | Established / established |

For age four the one-sided lower bound is −9.07 points, excluding both allowed losses. Age two's lower bound is −33.54 points: it is neither shown inferior nor shown non-inferior. Its seed differences are −24.22, +5.08 and −7.03 points, compared with −7.03, −0.39 and −0.39 for age four. There is no decision against age two.

The approved margin is **15 percentage points**, with **20 points the outer bound**. It was set beside the earlier keep-runtime control's two-run range of 13.67 points; that separate control's final three-run range is 26.56 points and is never pooled with these abort controls. The same-runtime control has SD 5.04 points and range 9.77 points. Paired-difference SDs are 3.83 points for age four and 14.72 for age two; achieved power at the 15/20-point margins is 98.9%/100.0% and 32.9%/46.8%, respectively. The pre-observation unpaired assumption gave 52.6%/71.2%. These powers assume a true difference of zero. Both arms have only three seeds and two degrees of freedom: the sample cannot distinguish a consistently tight configuration from a lucky draw.

| Chosen age-four configuration versus synchronous control | Audited observation | Confidence interval |
|---|---|---|
| Training wall, three matched seeds | **54.72% less**; mean wall 6,352.947 → 2,876.936 seconds | Retrospective 95% interval **[50.34%, 58.72%]** reduction |
| GPU-hours within the same training window, 40 H100s | **54.72% fewer**, exactly proportional to wall | Same **[50.34%, 58.72%]** interval; excludes allocation outside the window |
| Full task GPU-hours, seed 17 | 76.724753 → 40.303989; **47.47% fewer** | Not estimated from this single matched run |
| Control training wall, seeds 17 / 29 / 43 | 6,234.936 / 6,481.903 / 6,342.002 seconds | Included in the three-seed wall comparison |
| Age-four training wall, seeds 17 / 29 / 43 | 2,942.138 / 2,904.269 / 2,784.402 seconds | Included in the three-seed wall comparison |
| Age-four all-attempt task GPU-hours, seeds 17 / 29 / 43 | 40.303989 / 40.447218 / 38.710644 | Full matched-seed task-cost interval **unestimated**; control seed 29 lacks final accounting |

Training wall spans update one's start through update 100's cycle. The earlier comment's 52.81% was seed 17 alone; 54.72% is the three-seed estimate on the same definition. The wall estimate and interval use the geometric mean of three matched-seed ratios and a two-sided Student-t interval on their logarithms, with two degrees of freedom; the displayed mean seconds are arithmetic means. This is a retrospective descriptive interval, conditional on the measured configurations and scheduling periods. Three seeds cannot test its distributional assumption, and the pairs were not randomized concurrent trials.

Training-window GPU-hours equal wall seconds × 40 / 3,600, so their relative reduction and interval are identical to wall; they do not estimate full task cost. Full task GPU-hours include all individual allocations, setup and teardown. Seed 29's age-four startup preemption contributes 0.739367 GPU-hours to its 40.447218 total. Its control remained allocated on all five original tasks at the 10:58 UTC read, with no finish times or final accounting; the three-seed full task-GPU-hour interval therefore remains unestimated. Operational retries are not pooled into quality trajectories, and the entire campaign's cost is not inferred from successful attempts. The seed-17 47.47% full-task reduction remains labelled as one run.

The chosen run uses 32 Megatron learner GPUs and eight inference GPUs, one update per batch, 160 generation workers, buffer 32 and four responses per training prompt. Weight copies use the qualified expert-block path with expensive proofs disabled after qualification. The mask uses required rollout log probabilities, ratio bounds 0.5 and 5, veto 1e-5, no renormalization and no TIS. Response-token-weighted realised age is p50 3, p95 4 and maximum 4 in all three age-four runs; masked-token fractions are 0.170717%, 0.152229% and 0.171194%. The seed-17 synchronous control has age 0 throughout and 0.160394% masked tokens, near zero.

**What this means.** The measured operating envelope is **configured age 0–4 on the studied deep-pool family**, with **four the supported asynchronous operating point, two unresolved and one running**. This is not proof that every intervening age is safe. Workers and buffering change with the age allowance, so the comparison prices the complete bundle; it is not quality-neutral and does not isolate staleness alone. The cadence stays one. `regular_mask` wins the selector and is chosen for robustness; the experiment does not establish that it is universally better.

The negatives remain part of the result:

| Lever and class | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Keep pause, T | Not adopted: it failed its pre-registered wall gate, saving 2.1% of wall to update 25 (769.8 → 753.6 seconds) against the required 10%. Abort resubmits interrupted answers with their tokens and sampled log probabilities; cache re-prefill is the lost work. Keep's likelihood reference and admission behavior prevent a quality-neutral claim. Age-two keep did not complete operationally. No measured token-discard percentage or fixed quality penalty is attributed to it. |
| More inference engines, T | No accepted joint wall-time/resource improvement. The three-engine proof-subtracted calculation still fails its joint gate and is not a measured proofs-off run. Retain eight inference GPUs. |
| Speculation, T | The measured core and tail-latency tradeoff misses its joint gate; leave it off. |
| Partial rollouts, T | Native consumed-prompt identity qualification failed; the dependent comparison is offloaded, not a measured quality loss. |
| Engine knobs, X/T candidates | No joint speed candidate qualified; the frozen reward-veto audit is not evaluable. Keep defaults. |
| BF16/FP16 gradients, T | Snowball BF16 reduces memory but slows the measured training phase; no speed adoption. Dense FP16's three-seed fit supports no adoption, while its specific scientific kill does not fire. Snowball FP16 was not implemented for the measured pipeline/expert layout and was not run. |
| Cost-model fit, R | Coverage and independent prediction checks do not validate an optimum or a split recommendation. |
| Tensor-parallel decode with degree two, T | Excluded by the placement rule, not an additional measured negative. |
| Sixteen-learner geometry, T/R | Tested FP32/BF16 recipes exhausted memory before a completed update. No current transport/performance qualification; the conditional longer pair was not run. FSDP2 remains unqualified under its failed literal identity gate. |

Exact improvements are available separately from the configuration tradeoff:

- **X, ready for adoption:** [pause handshake](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/00f32e2b83c687d4770473005beee015e5e9559f), with [Marin counterpart](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/aead8ed03c909adefadc622bf7d92cc682de65a7). `K7_ROOT_NATIVE_GATE_PASS measured_syncs=20 pause_p50_seconds=0.10705400840379298 conservation=true engine_deaths=0 admission_stamps=1972`. The accompanying first-token admission policy is a ruled semantics change, not part of the exactness claim.
- **X, ready for adoption:** [expert-block transfer and full receiver-byte proof](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/501216e25ce07ed3046930404a7005ef619b3594), [Marin counterpart](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/027a4ee1c69b657c02f5e39f280d6549cf59cf94). `K10_TWENTY_PUBLICATION_AUDIT_PASS`: both 32/8 and 32/16 geometries have full coverage and zero mismatches; install p50 is 0.5088 and 0.5452 seconds. These are installation intervals, not full training-step speedups; the 16/24 row is unqualified.
- **X, ready for adoption:** [outside-pause diagnostics](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/d741cd3a34a7750d8c1901b57c381d9bc9921e2e). `OPTIMAL_SYNC_SHARED_INTEGRATION_PASS base=46e932e8 candidate=d741cd3a commits=2 files=7 affected_tests=171 lint=true source_weight_sync_exact=942e9123 outside_pause_default=true proofs_gate_retained=true marin_counterpart_already_shared=true`. Proofs-off adds no byte-equality evidence; retain the earlier proofs-on qualification.
- **X, ready for adoption:** [receipt-digest verification](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/466ba189337eab4fc36b772963e03de3a2c86f5e), **pending the maintainer's merge**. `S2S_CANDIDATE1_REPEAT_PASS`: the two paired full-call p50 reductions are 1.102562 and 1.708934 seconds (23.6% and 35.6%); full-call p95 improves in both. The byte gate has zero mismatches over 168 replay rows. The first pair's paused-interval increase reverses on repeat. The aggregate call is the decision metric under the amended rule; this candidate was not in the confirmation runtime.
- **X, ready for adoption:** [bounded S3 staging recovery](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/2dd25c169fff2676590795ca9c3db8d1d9cbc548). `E61_STAGE2_STAGING_RETRY_MUTATION_PASS old_no_retry_rejected=true mutation_in_memory=true source_unchanged=true`. It preserves completed files, removes partial bytes and fails after bounded exhaustion.
- **X, ready for adoption in its qualified scope:** [parameter remainders](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/aadd4d109ba3dd81cd98d8b7015d69f2a4209732). `K14_ROOT_RETAINED_AUDIT_PASS ranks=2 updates=10 cells=4 receipt_joins=20 mismatches=0`. The synthetic FP32-moment replay saves two bytes per owned parameter; it does not qualify Snowball or BF16-moment equivalence.

Every program-level kill criterion has a disposition:

| Criterion | Evaluation |
|---|---|
| 1. Sync plus wait below 15% of core | **False**: proof-subtracted shares are 73.646683% at 32/8, within-run 95% interval [64.843132%, 78.844274%], and 74.640969% at 32/16, [68.401215%, 78.421549%]. These exploratory adjustments preserve the observed schedule; no causal proofs-off replay is claimed. The no-headroom reduction does not fire. |
| 2. MoE knee at age at most one | **Not evaluable: MoE rung offloaded.** No knee or routing-replay qualification is inferred. |
| 3. Nontermination cannot be bounded | **Stage-three condition failed:** truncation was never below 10% at any scored point, with the control ending at 94.14% and the other completed run reaching 94.53%. The follow-on loss-aggregation failure required by the full compound kill is not measured. No fixed answer contract or held-out quality guarantee follows from the development endpoint. |
| 4. Two consecutive small-model winners fail confirmation | **Not established:** no audited pair of the specified consecutive winner-to-confirmation failures exists; the intermediate MoE ladder was offloaded. This does not validate small-model transfer. |
| 5. Uninformative experiments need redesign | **Applied as a design rule:** repeated setup/restore failures were recorded operationally and their configuration or packaging repaired, rather than counted as scientific results. No GPU-hour cost kill remains. Whole-campaign spend is not fully reconciled and is not asserted. |

**Next.** Investigate late-training instability and the failed stopping criterion first. Both completed stopping-qualification runs peak early and subsequently collapse; the endpoint and wider margin do not fix that. The proposed parser-under-crediting cause was withdrawn after the retained timeline showed the disagreement disappearing before collapse. Parser normalization still needs alignment with the frozen contract before another campaign.

Append the running age-one confirmation, retained-checkpoint held-out panels and buffer-pin twin as separate follow-ups. They do not hold this scoped development conclusion. Final native allocation accounting and the full task-GPU-hour interval remain to be completed. The original held-out-quality goal is not claimed demonstrated by development evaluations alone.

The offload list retains the MoE rung and its milestone; routing replay; stratified age/replay work; partial-rollout qualification; Snowball FP16 and smaller-learner/FSDP2 qualification; overlap and lossless-delta polish; the native evaluation prerequisite's unexplained crashes; consumption-time token-weighted telemetry gaps; verifier/parser normalization and the three frozen-harness compatibility walls; fixed-evaluation-seed follow-up; missing allocation endpoints and lifecycle-tool representation gaps. Approximate FP8/LoRA weight shipping remains discarded. These are explicit uncompleted or declined directions, not silent passes.

<details><summary>Provenance</summary>

The posted confirmation and stopping-qualification comments linked above were read directly. Exact source hashes and numerical bindings are retained with the audited records behind this report.

Confirmation runtime `ba5ba17100d77be97a6fc9f9aa5e4197bd24bccc`; Marin `a453edb92b14da9a8406c005f6bc4c76d72bc34b`; seeds 17/29/43, 100 updates, H100, P32/I8, C1/N1, abort, parser-only and regular mask. The control has 64 workers and no asserted explicit buffer override; age two/four have 96/160 workers and buffer 32. The development membership hash is `d8786335f86076dd5a7c73c12ec8ce176705533dae19648ceb9e22c31b4ce096`.

Quality is the authorized direct recomputation from pinned-tokenizer native dumps, with frozen correctness conjoined with accepted stop, verified membership and runtime-metric cross-checks. No `records.parquet` or semantic result is produced by this path. Primary family intervals use 10,000 seed-and-question bootstrap draws, seed 1729, alpha 0.05, Bonferroni simultaneous percentile intervals with Holm-adjusted p-values. They are not Holm intervals. The non-inferiority lower bound is a separate one-sided t procedure.

The frozen held-out battery contains all 3,294 accepted questions, id hash `82163b0ea8723ea99642473addc40c8e91e2c11a5d0f2714abd2c51174d4f57f`, parquet hash `4bff4f44609bbff2f0427aa744db379528325c608bfd5da74827f401adf33bde`. Panels use four responses per question, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95 and each checkpoint's training seed. Only the initial panel is scored: 3,012/13,176 = 22.860% frozen completed correctness beside runtime 2,812/13,176 = 21.342%. The 200 normally terminated answers differ through boxed/numerical formatting rejected by the runtime parser; parity fails. This is not a trained-checkpoint comparison. Update-100 panels remain follow-up work.

Primary evidence: the three-seed confirmation scoring receipt; the stage-three truncation join; the parser-rejection timeline; the four native terminal audits of the E9.1 and E9.2 members; the matched-seed performance-interval audit; the proof-subtracted sync-share recovery; the linked capability receipts; the retained offload register; and, for the receipt-digest candidate, its adoption and repeat-pair records. These retain gate-only proof costs separately from production timing.

</details>

🤖 Age cap one is unresolved at three matched seeds; the configuration is now running at eleven matched pairs

**What we did and why.** The [confirmation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5662695626) covered age caps zero, two and four. Age cap one — staleness 1 — was added as a fourth configuration at three seeds: the same runtime, a deep pool with 64 generation workers and buffer 32, abort at the weight copy, the parser-only stopping package, the mismatch-masking correction, and training seeds 17, 29 and 43. After the first two seeds' paired spread came in above the pre-registered 8-point escalation threshold, five more seeds were submitted, then matched synchronous controls at those same seeds, then three further pairs, for eleven matched pairs in all. The reported seed count is the number of complete pairs — an arm seed and its matched synchronous control, both at update 100 and both passing the membership gate — at the reporting moment.

**Results — age cap one, interim at three matched pairs.** Same 256-question development set, one response per question, update-100 endpoint, completed correctness (correct answer with an accepted stopping reason).

| Seed | Synchronous control | Age cap one | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 17 | 50.781% | 48.438% | −2.34 pp |
| 29 | 43.750% | 56.250% | +12.50 pp |
| 43 | 53.516% | 35.938% | −17.58 pp |
| **Mean** | **49.35%** | **46.88%** | **−2.47 pp** |

The fixed-observed-seed interval is [−5.60, +0.78] points with Holm p 0.130; the primary population interval, resampling seeds and questions, is [−16.80, +11.85] points with Holm p 0.742. The one-sided lower bound is −27.83 points, which excludes neither allowed loss. Non-inferiority is **not established at 15 or at 20 points**. Achieved power at three pairs is **32.1% at 15 points and 45.6% at 20**, from a paired-difference SD of 15.04 points; the pre-observation unpaired 10-point basis would have read 52.6% / 71.2%.

Stated plainly: age cap one is **not shown inferior, not shown non-inferior, and under-powered at three seeds**.

The method observation is the part worth carrying, and it is not the level. This configuration's point estimate, −2.47 points, and age cap four's, −2.60 points, are the same level to within a tenth of a point. Age cap four resolved non-inferiority at 15 points because its three seeds agree to within 6.6 points; age cap one resolves nothing because its three seeds span 30.1 points. **The seed count a configuration needs is a property of that configuration, not of the protocol.** The caution that goes with it: −2.47 points on three seeds with this scatter is a weak point estimate, and the eleven-pair result may move it in either direction.

On the scatter itself: age caps one and two scatter alike (paired SDs 15.04 and 14.72 points), and age caps zero and four are tight (5.04 points for the control's own spread, 3.83 points paired for age four). That ordering is **not established** on three seeds each. The ratio of the widest to the tightest paired variance is 15.4, with a one-sided p of 0.061 on an F(2,2) reference — two degrees of freedom on each estimate. No mechanism is offered for the pattern; the first hypothesis is that there is nothing to explain, and the eleven-pair data tests it directly.

Seed 29's run absorbed one preemption. Its integrity was checked before its number was read: every panel at updates 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 carries exactly 256 questions with one sample each, question ids match the frozen battery at every step, and the recomputation agrees exactly with the runtime aggregate from update 20 through update 100.

**Results — the buffer-pin twin.** The buffer-pin comparison lacked a same-shape reference with the buffer left unset, so one was run: the same packet with the group-buffer pin removed and nothing else changed. Copy every update, age cap one, 64 workers, abort, seed 17, 25 updates, the same runtime as the buffer-pin run.

| Measure | Pinned buffer 32 | Buffer unset |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total cycle time, 25 updates | 1,110.1 s | 1,111.1 s (+0.1%) |
| Mean staleness | 0.5312 | 0.5312 |
| Rejected rate | 0 | 0 |

Per-update medians differ by 5-10% in both directions — a slower median cycle alongside a higher token rate — which is distribution shape inside known run-to-run spread rather than a difference in total work. **Pinning the buffer alone changed nothing at this shape.** The deep pool's speed advantage in the earlier comparisons comes from the age allowance and the worker count, and it is paid for in realised answer age. One run per configuration and one seed: this bounds the pin's effect rather than measuring it.

**Results — the first held-out panel.** The frozen held-out battery is 3,294 questions, MATH levels 3 to 5 with MATH-500 removed, accepted-id SHA256 `82163b0e…`. It was scored at K=4 on the untrained step-630 weights. Membership is exact: 13,176 responses, four per question. Completed correctness under the frozen contract is **0.22860** overall, and 0.34302 / 0.23433 / 0.12447 by level, monotone in difficulty; truncation is 0.3249.

The runtime's own aggregate reads **0.21342**. Both numbers travel together. The 1.52-point gap is 200 responses; 262 rows of 13,176 (2.0%) disagree in total, all in one direction, where the frozen contract accepts a boxed or otherwise differently formatted correct answer that the runtime parser rejects. This is an artefact of the starting checkpoint's boxing habit, which trains out: the disagreement is gone by update 20 in every run examined. No W&B reference exists for this panel, so the parity check is dump-only and is reported as such. Update-100 held-out panels remain pending behind a checkpoint-load memory fix.

**What this means.** Nothing in the [milestone claim](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5663169886) changes. Age cap four still stands as the supported asynchronous operating point at the 15-point margin. Age caps one and two are both unresolved at three seeds, and no decision against either follows. The deep pool's speed gain is not free — it is bought with realised answer age, not with the buffer pin. Held-out evidence at update 100 is still pending, so the scoped development-set conclusion is unchanged and no held-out quality claim is made.

**Next.** The eleven-pair wave is running: sixteen jobs were queued at batch priority between 12:09 and 12:18 UTC, the reported N will be the number of complete pairs, and the wording is pre-registered for each outcome. Then the update-100 held-out panels on retained checkpoints, and the second weight-transfer candidate. Each is reported as a further comment; none of them holds this scoped development conclusion.

🤖 Milestone 7: Keep 32 Snowball learner GPUs; the tested 16-GPU recipes did not fit

**What we did and why.** Building on the [weight-sync milestone](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5652831170), we combined the earlier small-model precision screen and smaller-learner failures with the subsequent Snowball gradient and alternative-backend results to make the learner-size decision. The question is whether less learner memory can free GPUs for generation and deliver faster Snowball training at the same answer quality. We measured memory and training time separately from answer quality, because a smaller buffer alone does not establish a faster or equally capable training configuration.

Optional [backend and gradient configuration support](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/877d666923bec00329213b93b66ab2e7390a815e) remains opt-in; exact [placement configuration support](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/3093cf4adecdf30791c6c241068e9cab7953290c) is ready for adoption, with native memory and precision outcomes decided by the experiments below.

**Results.**

| Experiment | Audited result | Decision and scope |
|---|---|---|
| [Optimizer-state reduction on 32 learner GPUs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649671134) | Both arms completed five updates. Optimizer storage fell from 12 to 6 bytes per owned parameter; PPO peak allocated was 56.673 versus 55.382 GiB. Memory thresholds and retained learner identity pass. | Pass under the amended criterion described below; no quality-equivalence or smaller-learner claim. |
| Smaller learner with [FP32 gradients](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649672213) and [BF16 gradients](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649672315) | All four 16-learner / 24-inference-GPU arms exhausted memory in the first optimizer step, with zero completed updates. | Drop these measured recipes. They produced no update-level transport qualification, steady-state timing or fitted throughput prediction. |
| [Snowball gradient comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5653217865) at 32 learner / 8 inference GPUs | Over 20 updates, FP32 → BF16 PPO peak allocated was 57.654356 → 51.669019 GiB; training-phase time was 197.532683 → 210.388233 seconds, **6.508062% slower**. | BF16 is a memory lever, with no demonstrated training-speed benefit or precision selection. |
| [Dense FP16 runtime qualification](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649779657) | Four H100s completed three finite updates and one deliberately injected overflow with unanimous skip, backoff and recovery. | Qualifies the tested dense runtime prerequisite, without qualifying Snowball's pipeline and expert layout or full-model quality. |
| [FSDP2 on 32 learner GPUs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5652989341) | Five updates completed; all 32 learner ranks passed memory coverage, with PPO peak allocated 38.596513 GiB. Behavior exact-unit and zero-clipping tests failed at every update; retained learner identity passed. | Preserve the literal scientific failure. FSDP2 remains unadopted; no matched backend speed comparison or 16-GPU qualification. |

The earlier [Qwen precision screen](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5638672900) covered 33 arm-seeds across eleven families. Its original three-seed Megatron BF16-gradient comparison had completed-correctness delta **+0.91 percentage points, 95% interval [−1.95, +3.78]**, against FP32. This is the historical paired-question bootstrap conditional on those seeds, with no seed-population inference; it is not the final multiplicity-adjusted gradient comparison. The screen's [addendum](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5639039203) records a non-discriminating gradient-norm criterion and missing optimizer-moment and measured-model parameter-equality operands. FSDP2's seed volatility and missing changed-element instrumentation prevent a rounding-lever qualification.

The final Qwen three-way comparison adds FP16 gradients with dynamic loss scaling to the reused FP32 and BF16 controls, on three training seeds. At optimizer update 100, mean completed correctness is **61.72% for FP32, 62.63% for BF16 and 58.20% for FP16**. BF16 minus FP32 is **+0.911 percentage points**, with an interval spanning zero. FP16 minus FP32 is **−3.516 points**:

| Inference for FP16 minus FP32 | Simultaneous interval (percentage points) | Holm-adjusted p-value |
|---|---:|---:|
| Conditional on the three observed seeds | [−7.031, 0.000] | 0.0574 |
| Resampling training seeds and questions | [−15.234, +5.859] | 0.9363 |

These are Bonferroni simultaneous percentile intervals for the two-comparison family, with Holm-adjusted p-values. The earlier two-seed FP16 estimate was positive; adding seed 43 reverses its sign. No non-finite step was observed, and although the point estimate is worse than the two-point margin, the final interval does not exclude zero, so the specific FP16 kill—any non-finite step, or a loss greater than two points with an interval excluding zero—does not fire. **FP16 adoption is unsupported.** BF16 and FP32 remain indistinguishable on this evidence; no BF16 superiority is established. FP16 seed 43 ends with 39.84% truncated answers, a warning carried alongside the aggregate result.

The three FP16 members have accepted final audited dispositions. The retained FP16 telemetry reports a 596,115,456-byte reduction buffer and loss scale 128, with no observed overflow or skipped optimizer update. Seed 43's authenticated, globally reduced telemetry covers all 100 optimizer minibatches; seeds 17 and 29 retain bounded raw-rank coverage. No fully audited three-way step-time comparison or exhaustive raw-rank inventory is asserted. Paired semantic quality is unavailable because the reused controls retain aggregate semantic means rather than per-question semantic outcomes; unresolved answers supply no semantic evidence.

The Snowball gradient pair used one seed and different realized trajectories. Completed-correct development answers went from 38/256 to 63/256 for FP32 and 42/256 to 27/256 for BF16, at updates zero and 20. These short-run harness counts have no confidence interval and select no precision. The smaller whole-run core time in the BF16 arm cannot be attributed to gradient precision: it consumed fewer tokens, and the arms already differed before training. Paired semantic quality is unavailable; unresolved answers contribute no semantic evidence.

**What this means.** Keep Megatron with 32 learner GPUs as the working trainer. The measured smaller-learner recipes failed before producing the required memory, weight-sync and current-cadence prediction evidence, so the conditional 25-update smaller-learner comparison was not run. Its recovered historical synchronous-cadence assumption also failed its threshold, but it is not a measured current throughput fit. The separate smaller FSDP2 learner remains **not run and unqualified** under the existing rule that an exact-unit identity failure stops further FSDP2 arms; stochastic/Kahan qualification is also absent. The unmatched backend timings do not evaluate the planned training-time kill.

The Megatron optimizer-state gate was explicitly amended to require **passing memory thresholds and retained learner identity**; both pass. Its original behavior-ratio failure remains diagnostic evidence. That amendment applies to this Megatron gate alone and does not change FSDP2's frozen failure. The four smaller-learner arms use different gradient or transport configurations, so they do not reject every possible configuration under the identical-repeat memory rule.

Keep precision choices as measured tradeoffs. Snowball FP16 was offloaded before composition because its pipeline and expert layout are unimplemented on the tested FP16 path; there is no Snowball FP16 run. The [parameter-remainders replay](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5649716093) retains exact synthetic evidence with FP32 moments; it supplies neither BF16-moment equivalence nor the missing measured-model precision operands.

Carry the measured negatives forward: more engines at age one, n-gram speculation, partial rollouts, small-model engine knobs, both smaller-learner gradient recipes and the standalone throughput curve supplied no adopted speed improvement. Tensor-parallel decode per engine, FP8 KV cache, larger maximum sequence counts and faster MoE kernels remain excluded by their recorded placement or implementation evidence; these are not additional GPU measurements. BF16 gradient reduction remains a memory option with the slower measured training phase above.

**Next.** Carry the working learner geometry and explicit precision limits into the [balance synthesis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5660856226) and the subsequent confirmation. The next numbered milestone is **system balance measured**.

**What we did and why.** Two more matched pairs, seeds 79 and 97, completed after the [three-seed interim](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8955#issuecomment-5663904792), so the statistic was recomputed on five complete arm-and-control pairs.
